title: Peak At Least Double the Rest
statement:
You get an array nums of non-negative integers in which the largest value appears exactly once.

The largest value dominates if it is at least twice as large as every other element. Return the index of the largest value if it dominates, and -1 otherwise. An array with one element is dominated by that element.

examples.why: 7 is at least 2 · 3 = 6, and the other values are smaller than 3.
9 is more than 2 · 2, but less than 2 · 5 = 10. Only the runner-up matters.

hints: You do not need to compare the largest value with every other element. Which one other element decides the answer?
If the largest value is at least twice the second largest, it is at least twice everything smaller too.
Track the largest value, its index and the second largest in a single pass.

explain.intuition:
Checking the maximum against every other element works, but only one comparison really matters: the second largest value. If the peak is at least twice the runner-up, it is at least twice everything below the runner-up too.

So one pass is enough. Keep the largest value with its index and the second largest. When a new value beats the largest, the old largest becomes the runner-up. When it only beats the runner-up, replace the runner-up.
steps: For each i: if nums[i] > best, move best into second, then set best = nums[i] and idx = i.
pitfalls: Forgetting to move the old maximum into second when a new maximum appears. In [5, 9] the runner-up is 5.
Using > instead of ≥. Exactly double dominates.
Returning the value instead of its index.

solutions.title: Find the maximum, then check everyone
solutions.idea: Two passes: locate the maximum, then make sure no other element is more than half of it.

solutions.title: Track the top two in one pass
solutions.idea: Only the runner-up can stop the peak from dominating.

followups: The largest value may now appear more than once. What should the rules be, and what changes in the code?
Find the k largest values in one pass when k is small. What structure keeps the top k?
lcTitle: Largest Number At Least Twice of Others
